s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive respiratory distress and cardiovascular compromise in a young calf
salient_findings: Severe dilation of the right atrium and right ventricle
Hypoplastic left ventricle with reduced mitral valve orifice
key_facts: 10-day-old, 40-kg male Chianina calf
Temperature 38.5 °C
Heart rate 170 beats/min with regular rhythm
Respiratory rate 60 breaths/min
Jugular pulses present
Mucous membranes cyanotic, especially after exertion
Grade IV/VI right apical systolic murmur
Harsh bronchovesicular lung sounds
Sinus tachycardia at 170 beats/min on electrocardiography
Severe tricuspid regurgitation and bidirectional shunting at septal defects

salient_findings: Severe dilation of the right atrium and right ventricle
Hypoplastic left ventricle with reduced mitral valve orifice
key_facts: 10-day-old, 40-kg male Chianina calf
Temperature 38.5 °C

Severe tricuspid regurgitation and bidirectional shunting at septal defects

differentials: Congenitally Corrected Transposition of the Great Arteries
per_call: Congenitally Corrected Transposition of the Great Arteries

shortlist.label: Double Outlet Right Ventricle
shortlist.why_kept: Two great vessels arising in parallel from the right ventricle

shortlist.label: Tricuspid Atresia
shortlist.why_kept: Severe tricuspid regurgitation and bidirectional shunting at septal defects

shortlist.label: Tetralogy of Fallot
shortlist.why_kept: Cyanosis, harsh bronchovesicular lung sounds, and severe dilation of the right atrium and ventricle

shortlist.label: Hypoplastic Left Heart Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Markedly hypoplastic left ventricle with a severely reduced mitral valve orifice

shortlist.label: Ebstein's Anomaly
shortlist.why_kept: Severe tricuspid regurgitation and right atrial dilation

raw.rationale: The presence of two great vessels arising in parallel from the right ventricle, severe dilation of the right atrium and right ventricle, and bidirectional shunting at septal defects support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Tricuspid Atresia
rejected.why: The presence of severe tricuspid regurgitation suggests that the tricuspid valve is not atretic.

rejected.label: Tetralogy of Fallot
rejected.why: The case lacks mention of pulmonary stenosis, a key component of Tetralogy of Fallot.

rejected.label: Hypoplastic Left Heart Syndrome
rejected.why: While the left ventricle is hypoplastic, the primary issue is the double outlet from the right ventricle, not the underdevelopment of the left heart.

rejected.label: Ebstein's Anomaly
rejected.why: The description does not include the characteristic downward displacement of the tricuspid valve into the right ventricle seen in Ebstein's Anomaly.
